fields.description: The deepest rung a society still registers records at. Marking a level here moves the marker: whichever active level held it is unset in the same save, so adding a deeper tier is one edit rather than two. At most one active level carries it. Inactive levels are exempt and keep whatever they had.
fields.label: Is Lowest Level

fields.description: A Geo Node at this level must be filed under a parent node. The parent has to sit at a shallower level, which is refused if it does not. Skipping a rung, for example a ward straight under a region, is allowed and only warns: some societies genuinely have no tier in between.
fields.label: Requires Parent

fields.description: An inactive level keeps its records but drops out of the ladder: it is left out of the hierarchy overview, its number is free for another level to take, and it neither claims nor loses the lowest marker.
fields.label: Is Active

fields.description: Where this level sits in the ladder. 1 is the top, and each rung below it counts up. A new level is pre filled with the next free number, so you rarely type one. This is presentation and a data entry guide: the tree decides structure, and nothing about ancestry, routing or scope reads this number. Reusing a number is allowed and only warns, because two societies on one site each number their own ladder from 1.
fields.label: Geo Level Order

fields.description: The ladder as it stands, read at the moment this form opened. The top rung is derived from the lowest active order and is deliberately not a field on this doctype: a stored flag would be a third answer to where the hierarchy begins, alongside this order and the parentage of the nodes themselves.
fields.label: Hierarchy
